purpose: Teach: 酸味/聞き手/山脈/晩餐/人魚/占星術/静脈/堤防

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはお茶の酸味を楽しまれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he really appreciated the tartness of good tea.
lines.style: Soft, drifting voice as if surfacing from a distant memory. Gentle opening on the address. Slow pace, allowing space between phrases. Warmth edged with something irretrievable.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、聞き手としてご立派でらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your father was such a good listener too, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm affirmation with a gentle upward lilt at the end. Tender and present, drawing him into shared remembering. Soft emphasis on 'good listener' — noticing what mattered to him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと山脈を見に旅行した
lines.en: Gran, I remember when he took me to see the mountains when I was young.
lines.style: Voice catches slightly on the memory. Measured, almost careful — preserving the weight of it. Breathing room between the setup and the detail. Eyes distant.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お祝いに晩餐をご家族と楽しまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He always loved celebrating with the family over a good dinner, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Affirming with a gentle warmth. Small smile in the voice — not correcting, but gently weaving in what she remembers. Slight lift on 'good dinner,' tender on the closing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが孫に人魚の絵本を読まれた
lines.en: Gran, when he was younger, he used to read picture books to the grandchildren — I still remember the mermaid story.
lines.style: Quieter now, more fragile. The memory of his tenderness lands carefully. Slight tremor on 'mermaid story' — the smallness of what endures. Trailing fade.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、占星術にも興味をお持ちでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He had such curiosity about things — even the stars, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gently echoing his tone, meeting him in the tenderness. 'Curiosity' spoken with warmth and recognition. The 'didn't he' is a soft invitation back into shared knowing, not a question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは静脈の血を採られたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was ill, they had to draw blood from his veins. I was there with him.
lines.style: The lightness drops. Voice becomes steadier, more present — witnessing, not wallowing. Clinical detail spoken with quiet dignity. Brief pause before the last phrase. Protective tone toward his father's vulnerability.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、堤防沿いの桜を毎春楽しまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And every spring, without fail, he'd go see the cherry blossoms by the embankment, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: Soft closing voice, almost a whisper. Affectionate certainty — she knew him too, after all. The 'wouldn't he' is intimate, not interrogative. Gentle trailing-off, like settling back into shared peace.
